en: The Apadāna of the Elder Aṅkolapupphiya Mandāravapupphiya Chapter 5.5 The Apadāna of the Elder Aṅkolapupphiya: I offered a flower from the aṅkola tree to the Buddha Vipassī, who was seated upon his seat. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. Having passed away from there, I was born here in this world. I am now known as Aṅkolapupphiya; I have attained the state of an Arhat. My final existence has been reached; there will be no further birth. This is my last body; I shall not be subject to further becoming. I have abandoned all defilements; I am free from all suffering. I have attained the destruction of craving; I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra. I have reached the goal; I have accomplished what was to be done. I have laid down the burden; I am liberated through perfect knowledge. I have attained the supreme, peaceful state of Nibbāna.

“The Fully Enlightened One named Paduma was then dwelling on Cittakūṭa;
Having seen the aṅkola tree in full bloom,
Having approached the Fully Enlightened One,
the Conqueror, I offered a lotus flower.
Whatever flower I offered in worship,
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Aṅkolapupphiya spoke these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Aṅkolapupphiya.
